About the tune

  • Music (1902): William James Kirkpatrick (1838–1921)

Metre: 8.4.8.4.7.7.7.4 +.8.8.4.8.8.4.

Melody from the Christian Classics Ethereal Hymnary (CCEH, public domain); tune WHEN LOVE SHINES IN by William James Kirkpatrick (1838–1921). The CCEH gives its tunes as four-part scores; this page has the melody only, read from its MIDI file and checked against its incipit, and NoteFusion's engine wrote the solfa from the notes. It has not yet been checked against a printed hymn book.

Questions about When Love Shines In

What is the doh of When Love Shines In?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does When Love Shines In start on?

It starts on d (E♭ in Eb major). Find doh first, then sing up or down to d.

What words can be sung to When Love Shines In?

When Love Shines In is in the metre 8.4.8.4.7.7.7.4 +.8.8.4.8.8.4: lines of 8, 4, 8, 4, 7, 7, 7, 4,, then, 8, 8, 4, 8, 8, 4 syllables. Words written in the same metre fit it; check where the stresses fall before you sing them together.

Is When Love Shines In in the public domain?

Yes. William James Kirkpatrick died in 1921; the tune was first published in 1902. Everyone named died before 1955 and it was published before 1929, so the tune is out of copyright in Nigeria, the UK, the EU and the United States. Modern arrangements of it can still be under copyright.
